# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The incumbent is timing-feasible at WNS 0.553 ns and WHS 0.135 ns, with 7 LUTs and 9 FFs; the objective is strictly fewer LUTs while retaining timing feasibility. The seed uses a 32-bit counter for a modulo-256 PWM period, though the incumbent’s 9 FFs suggest synthesis may already prune its unused upper state. Top numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric latency annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Using an 8-bit counter that wraps naturally at 255 may remove the terminal-count comparator and counter-input mux, reducing LUT use while preserving the modulo-256 sequence.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the 32-bit counter with an 8-bit counter and remove the explicit `counter == 255` reset branch, relying on 8-bit increment overflow for modulo-256 wrap. Keep the synchronous active-high reset of both counter and `pwm_out`, and keep `pwm_out` registered from the comparison of the pre-increment counter against the zero-extended `duty`. The expected LUT reduction must be confirmed by routed reports; promote only if simulation and all metric gates pass and LUT use is strictly below 7 with WNS and WHS both nonnegative.
